content: The EXSCEL trial evaluated the effects of the once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide on cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes. However, the findings of this trial did not achieve statistical significance. Despite this, there is robust evidence supporting the cardiovascular benefits of both GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), those with multiple cardiovascular risk factors, or individuals with diabetic kidney disease. Meta-analyses have demonstrated that GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors are capable of reducing the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events, lowering hospitalization rates, and improving clinical outcomes in high-risk diabetic populations.
